subject: Confirmation: prompt & output storage, retention, residency
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@brighthealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-30T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + next steps on prompt/output handling and residency

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of what I heard and the actions we discussed so we can make sure we’re aligned: 

- Primary ask: BrightHealth will be sending user-generated content that may include personal health information (PHI). You need assurance that prompts/outputs containing PHI are not retained beyond what is strictly necessary for inference and troubleshooting.
- Residency: production inference must run and store any persistent telemetry only in US regions (preference: us-east-1). No EU/APAC storage for BrightHealth data.
- Retention: you asked for short-term troubleshooting logs; you mentioned 90 days as a conservative cap but are open to shorter windows if possible.
- Redaction: you want automatic PII/PHI redaction at ingestion if Redwood stores any prompt/output for sampling or QA.
- Contractual: SOC 2 + a DPA that references data residency and custom retention windows.

Can you confirm or correct the above bullets? If that is correct, I’ll loop in our security lead (Rishi) and send the current retention matrix and a DPA draft for review. I’ve attached the security whitepaper and the retention matrix for context.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm whether 90 days is an absolute requirement or a maximum (we can propose 60/30 as options).
2) We’ll schedule a 30-minute security review with Rishi to walk through technical controls and deployment options (hosted vs Dedicated/Private).
3) If Dedicated/Private is required for PHI workloads, we’ll provide an implementation timeline and kitted costs.

Thanks —

Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0196
redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redwood-security-whitepaper.pdf, data-retention-matrix.xlsx
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@brighthealth.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps on prompt/output handling and residency

Hi Dylan —

Thanks for the summary — that matches the conversation closely. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Residency: US-only is a hard requirement for production PHI. We prefer us-east-1 but can accept us-west-2 as fallback.
- Prompts/Outputs: We need guarantees that prompts and full model outputs containing PHI are not persisted to long-term storage on your hosted environment. We are open to ephemeral caching during inference, but persisted copies (for logging, QA, or sampling) must be removable or masked automatically.
- Retention: 90 days is our internal maximum for any telemetry that might contain PHI, but preferred window is 30 days if feasible. If Redwood can offer configurable retention per account (30/60/90) that would be ideal.
- Redaction & Sampling: We are willing to allow limited, opt-in sampling for model quality if those samples are redacted automatically and stored only in a dedicated, access-controlled bucket with encryption + restricted access list.
- Compliance artifacts: Please send SOC 2 Type II report and the DPA. We’ll also need an engineer-level contact to schedule a technical review with our security team tomorrow or early next week.

Olivia
Head of Product Security | BrightHealth AI
olivia@brighthealth.ai
+1 617 555 0142
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@brighthealth.ai>
Date: 2026-07-30T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightHealth — confirmation + technical ask (retention/residency)

Rishi —

Looping you in per Olivia’s reply. Key asks: US-only residency, configurable retention (pref 30d but max 90d), no persistent storage of prompts/outputs with PHI (unless redacted & access-controlled), KMS for encryption, and SOC 2/DPA.

Can you confirm our hosted default behavior and what we can promise in writing for a commercial contract? Also note Olivia’s request for an engineer-level technical review — can you or someone from your team do a 30-minute call tomorrow or Monday morning PST?

Thanks —
Dylan
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@brighthealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightHealth — confirmation + technical ask (retention/residency)

Hi Olivia, Dylan, Marissa —

Thanks — appreciate the clear summary. Below is a concise, factual response you can rely on for the commercial discussions. Happy to go deeper on the 30-minute security call; I’m available Monday 08:00–11:00 PST.

Redwood hosted (default) behavior
- Inference path: prompts and generated tokens are held in-memory or in ephemeral caches during inference and are not written to durable object storage by default.
- Operational logs: metadata (request timestamp, model id, token counts, routing decision) is retained for diagnostics and billing. Full-text request/response logs are NOT retained persistently by default in our hosted offering unless sampling is enabled.
- Sampling & QA: We support an opt-in sampling pipeline for QA and model quality. When enabled, samples are written to a dedicated, access-restricted bucket. We offer automatic PII/PHI redaction prior to persistence (removes/obfuscates common PHI patterns) as part of the sampling pipeline.
- Retention windows: Default operational metadata retention = 60 days. Full-text samples (if enabled) retention is configurable per-customer; options we support out-of-the-box: 30 days, 60 days, 90 days. We can commit to configuring BrightHealth to 30 days for samples if required.
- Residency: We can run inference and persist any sampled artifacts only in US regions (us-east-1 / us-west-2) for this account. We will include a contractual clause to enforce region restrictions for persistent storage.
- Encryption & key management: All persisted artifacts are encrypted at rest. For Dedicated/Private deployments we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. For hosted accounts we support Bring-Your-Own-KMS (BYOK) on an enterprise plan.
- Dedicated/Private option: If BrightHealth cannot accept any hosted persistence of full-text samples, the Dedicated or Private deployment option can be configured to disable persistent logging entirely and provide an air-gapped on-prem option.

Attachments: I’ve attached the SOC 2 summary and a DPA template (DPA_BrightHealth.docx). Also attached the retention matrix (data-retention-matrix.xlsx) that maps artifacts to default and configurable policies.

Contractual & next steps
1) We can commit to a configurable sample retention of 30 days for BrightHealth in the hosted product and a contractual residency clause limiting persistent storage to US regions.
2) If BrightHealth requires zero hosted persistence for any full-text prompts/outputs containing PHI, we recommend Dedicated/Private. I can scope timeline and costs after the call.
3) I will send the DPA via DocuSign for signature once we agree on retention/residency terms — draft link included here: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=na1&acct=abc123&pfId=0a1b2c3d

Please let me know what time on Monday works for the technical review. I’ll have a solutions engineer on the call to demonstrate redaction behavior and sampling controls.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com
